meta.description:
Wing Staff Agency personnel include the Wing Command Staff, Command Post, Inspector General, Safety, Public Affairs, Judge Advocate General, Chaplain Corps, and Comptroller Flight (Finance). These offices primarily perform administrative duties in an office environment. Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) findings and Bioenvironmental Engineering (BE) survey notes should address typical administrative hazards, including ergonomic stressors from prolonged computer use, slips/trips/falls, electrical hazards, office equipment use, emergency evacuation procedures, and workplace stress/fatigue.

Safety and Public Affairs personnel may be required to perform duties on the flightline and in areas containing moving vehicles, ground support equipment, and aircraft. Major hazards in these areas include aircraft operations, vehicle traffic, moving equipment, jet blast, prop/rotor wash, high noise levels, foreign object debris (FOD), uneven surfaces, weather exposure, and restricted operational areas.

Required controls include completion of required flightline and local safety training; use of appropriate personal protective equipment, including hearing protection and high-visibility apparel as required; compliance with flightline driving, pedestrian, FOD, and airfield procedures; maintaining situational awareness around aircraft and vehicles; use of designated walkways and safe stand-off distances; and coordination with the responsible airfield or maintenance organization before entering operational areas. Personnel will not enter restricted areas, approach operating aircraft, operate vehicles or equipment, or conduct photography/public affairs activities near aircraft without required authorization, training, and escort requirements as applicable.
meta.references:
Wing Staff Agency personnel will comply with all applicable Department of the Air Force Instructions (DAFIs), Department of the Air Force Manuals (DAFMANs), installation directives, and local operating procedures relevant to their assigned duties and work locations. Supervisors are responsible for ensuring personnel receive required training, understand applicable safety and emergency procedures, and comply with established workplace controls.

Where DAFI, DAFMAN, installation, or local guidance differs, personnel will follow the most restrictive applicable requirement unless otherwise directed by the appropriate authority. Personnel will notify their supervisor or unit safety representative of unclear requirements, unsafe conditions, or conflicts between procedures before proceeding with work.
List of Instruction applicable to the workplace is:
DAFMAN 91-203
DAFI 91-202
DAFI 91-207
DODI 6055.01
meta.jhaNotes:
Primary work hazards include:- Office ergonomics, including repetitive-motion, workstation, and manual-material-handling hazards.- Slips, trips, and falls from cords, wet floors, uneven surfaces, stairways, ladders, and elevated work.- Electrical hazards associated with office equipment, power strips, damanged cords, and unauthorized
equipment.- Fire, evacuation, severe weather, and emergency response hazards.- Cleaning chemical exposure, including disinfectants, bleach, and other common-area cleaning
products.- Noise, flying debris, high-pressure water, chemical splash, vibration, and struck-by hazards when
personnel volunteer or are assigned lawn-care, pressure-washing, facility-maintenance, or similar
support tasks.- Vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, parking-lot, and flight-line hazards when performing duties outside the
office area.
Applicable guidance and references:
Employees will follow applicable technical orders, job guides, manufacturer instructions, Safety Data
Sheets (SDS), approved work instructions, job orders, risk-management documentation (Deliberate
Risks Assessment Worksheets), and Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs), when applicable
meta.emergencyNumbers:
From Land line: 911

From cell phone: 301-981-9911In the event of a fire, medical emergency, security incident, hazardous condition, or other immediate threat to life or property, personnel will promptly contact emergency services.

From a landline: Dial 911.

From a cellular phone: Dial 301-981-9911.

When contacting emergency dispatch, remain calm and provide the following information:

Exact location, including building number, floor, room, or nearest identifiable landmark.

Nature of the emergency (e.g., medical emergency, fire, injury, aircraft-related hazard, suspicious activity, or hazardous material spill).

Number of personnel involved or injured and the apparent severity of injuries, if known.

Any immediate hazards present, such as fire, smoke, fuel, moving vehicles, aircraft operations, electrical hazards, or unsafe conditions.

A callback telephone number and point of contact, if available.

Personnel should not place themselves at risk while reporting an emergency. If safe to do so, notify nearby personnel, activate the appropriate alarm system, provide basic aid within the limits of training, and direct emergency responders to the location. Follow installation emergency procedures, evacuation routes, and instructions from emergency responders or designated building personnel.
meta.medicalFacility:
AGR personnel will use Malcolm Grow Medical Clinics and Surgery Center at Joint Base Andrews for routine medical care, treatment, and occupational health support. When performing duties at another military installation, personnel may use the local military treatment facility in accordance with installation procedures and eligibility requirements.

If medical assistance is required outside normal on-base clinic hours, personnel should seek care at a local emergency room or urgent care facility, as appropriate to the severity of the condition. For life-threatening emergencies, personnel should immediately call 911 from a landline or 301-981-9911 from a cellular phone.

On Base ER hours: 0700 to 1900 hours, 7 days a week.
meta.evacuationRoute:
Evacuation Routes and Assembly Areas
Fire: 
In the event of a fire or other evacuation emergency, personnel will immediately use the nearest safe, designated exit from their office or work area. Do not use elevators during a fire evacuation. If the primary exit is unsafe or inaccessible, use an alternate designated exit. After exiting the building, proceed to the Building 3252 parking lot and report to the designated representative for your office, workplace, or directorate for accountability. Remain at the assembly area until released or directed otherwise by emergency responders or designated building personnel.

Bomb Threat: 
In the event of a bomb threat, personnel will follow instructions announced through the Giant Voice system, building emergency notification system, or provided by emergency responders and building officials. When directed to evacuate, exit the building through the nearest safe, designated exit and proceed to the assembly area at the east-side running track section. Report to the designated accountability representative for your office, workplace, or directorate. Do not reenter the building or leave the assembly area until authorized by emergency responders or designated building personnel.
meta.shelterInPlace:
When directed to shelter in place, personnel will proceed to the designated shelter location in the lower level of Building 3252, Room 113. The room is located at the end of the hallway adjacent to the wing break room.

Personnel will follow instructions provided through the Giant Voice system, building emergency notification system, emergency responders, or designated building personnel. Remain in the shelter location until an all-clear is announced or personnel are directed to relocate.
meta.activeShooterMethods:
113TH WG defines an active-shooter/hostile-person situation as where an individual is actively engaged in killing or attempting to kill people in a confined and other populated area and continues until stopped by law enforcement, suicide, or intervention.
NOTIFICATION

1.	Notify bystanders of the emergency and dictate their assistance; direct an individual to call the SF call 9-1-1 from a land line or 301-981-9911 from cell phone and state the location; and remain on the line until situation is handled or becomes too hazardous to remain.
2.	Initiate the Pre-Accident Plan specific to the Squadron or flight ’s mission profile.

RESPONSE

1.	Run
a.	Have an escape route and plan in mind.
b.	Leave your belongings behind.
c.	Help others escape, if possible.
d.	Evacuate regardless of others.
e.	Warn/prevent individuals from entering.
f.	Do not attempt to move wounded people.
g.	Keep your hands visible.
h.	Follow police instructions.
i.	Call 9-1-1 when safe.
2.	Hide
a.	Lock doors.
b.	Hide behind large items (e.g., cabinet, desk) offering protection, if shots are fired.
c.	Out of the active shooter’s view.
d.	Silence cell phone/pager.
e.	Remain quiet.
f.	Do not restrict options for movement.
g.	Provide Law Enforcement with Information (if safe to do so)
	Location of shooters.
	Number of shooters.
	Physical description of shooters.
	Number and types of weapons.
	Number of potential victims.
3.	Fight (as last resort)
a.	Act as aggressively as possible.
b.	Throw items and use improvised weapons.
c.	Work together to incapacitate the shooter.
d.	Commit to your actions.

EVACUATION	

1.	Personnel are to evacuate the facility by the closest exit following published procedures.
2.	113TH WG representatives are to escort contractors and visitors.
3.	Supervisors are to verify their areas are clear of personnel.
4.	Personnel, temporary workers, contractors, and visitors are to report to an established assembly area and wait to be released.
5.	Supervisors and 113TH WG representatives will take accountability of their personnel, temporary workers, contractors, or visitors.  If personnel are not accounted for, UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE WILL PERSONNEL RETURN TO THE BUILDING.
6.	Supervisors and 113TH WG representatives will report accountability to their chain-of-command.
7.	Supervisors and 113TH WG representatives will report accountability to the law enforcement incident commander.
8.	During adverse climate weather and after accountability is complete, Supervisors and 113TH WG representatives will coordinate with the incident commander on options for personnel shelter.

REACTING TO LAW ENFORCEMENT
1.	Remain calm.
2.	Put down any items.
3.	Raise hands and spread fingers.
4.	Avoid quick movements.
5.	Avoid pointing, screaming, or yelling.
6.	Proceed in direction from which Security Forces personnel are entering.

RECOVERY
1.	The law enforcement incident commander will direct actions to those effected by the situation.
2.	The law enforcement incident commander will declare if the area is safe to return to operations.
3.	113TH WG will:
a.	Determine a method for notifying families.
b.	Assess psychological state of individuals.
c.	Identify and fill critical personnel or operational gaps.

REPORTING AND INVESTIGATION
The effected Squadron or flight Command will coordinate an After-Action Review with supervisors, USR’s, and security by completing:
1.	Appropriate incident forms.
2.	Initiate an incident investigation.
3.	Conduct an EAP evaluation.
4.	Conduct root-cause analysis and corrective-action development.
5.	Complete an AFSAS report, if appropriate, to be completed by the 113th Wing safety office qualified personnel.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter:
113TH WG defines a severe weather emergency as natural disasters including tornados, floods, mudslides, earthquakes, or severe weather (such as hail, lightning, extended snow, and thunderstorms) that results in property damage or serious risk of injury. Weather related emergencies might result in disruption of services or personal risk.

NOTIFICATION

1. The 113TH WG Staff Duty will maintain a weather-alert radio (or other real-time weather monitoring and notification process) and personnel will receive training on its use.
2. If a weather-alert is received:
a. The 113TH WG Staff Duty will notify subordinate Squadron or flights of the alert.
b. Subordinate Squadron or flight  commands will monitor the weather via computer or smartphone (or other real-time weather monitoring and notification process).
3. If the severe weather is headed towards the facility, 113TH WG Staff Duty will determine the necessity for shelter.
4. Initiate the Pre-Accident Plan specific to the Squadron or flight’s mission profile.

RESPONSE

If it is determined to shelter:
1. Equipment operators are to shut down their equipment in an orderly, safe, and expedited manner.
2. 113TH WG representatives are to escort contractors and visitors.
3. Supervisors are to verify their areas are clear of personnel.
4. Personnel, temporary workers, contractors, and visitors are to report to an established shelter and wait to be released.
5. Supervisors and 113TH WG representatives will take accountability of their personnel, temporary workers, contractors, or visitors.  If personnel are not accounted for, UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE WILL PERSONNEL LEAVE THE SHELTER.
6. Supervisors and 113TH WG representatives will report accountability to their chain-of-command.
7. Supervisors and 113TH WG representatives will report accountability to the emergency incident commander.

RECOVERY

1. USR’s will inventory shelter supplies and replenish those used.
2. Operators will bring equipment shut down during the incident back up to operation using normal procedures.

REPORTING AND INVESTIGATION

The effected Squadron or flight Command will coordinate an After-Action Review with supervisors, USR’s:

1. Appropriate incident forms.
2. Initiate an incident investigation.
3. Conduct an EAP evaluation.
4. Conduct root-cause analysis and corrective-action development.
5. Complete an AFSAS report, if appropriate, to be completed by the 113th Wing safety office qualified personnel.
meta.fireEquipmentNotes:
FIRE EXTINGUISHERS, AUTOMATED EXTERNAL DEFIBRILLATORS, AND FIRST AID KITS:

Personnel should familiarize themselves with the location of emergency equipment within Building 3252 and report missing, damaged, expired, or inaccessible equipment to the appropriate facility or safety representative.

Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) are located at the following locations:

Lower floor, near the Wing break room.

Auditorium entrance.

Second floor, to the left of the elevator.

In the event of a suspected cardiac emergency, immediately contact emergency services, send someone to retrieve the nearest AED, and provide care within the limits of your training until emergency responders arrive.

Fire extinguishers are located along building hallways and near designated exit routes. Personnel should only attempt to use a fire extinguisher when trained, the fire is small and contained, and a clear, safe exit route is available. If the fire cannot be safely controlled, evacuate immediately and contact emergency services.

Manual fire alarm pull stations are located along designated paths of egress, generally near exit doors. When a fire or smoke condition is identified, activate the nearest manual fire alarm pull station, if safe to do so; evacuate using the nearest safe exit; and report to the designated assembly area for accountability.

First aid kits are maintained in designated work areas. Personnel should use first aid kits for minor injuries only and seek appropriate medical assistance for injuries requiring further evaluation or treatment.
meta.safetyBoardLocation: The Wing information bulletin board is located in the Wing break room, Room 109. Personnel should review the bulletin board regularly for current safety information, emergency procedures, policy updates, training announcements, and other Wing notices.
meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
Traffic Safety, Local Hazards, and Vehicle Notes
Personnel who operate or ride in government-owned, rental, or privately owned vehicles for official duties at Joint Base Andrews (JBA) or throughout the Washington, DC, Maryland, and Virginia region will comply with applicable installation, federal, state, and local traffic laws; posted speed limits; parking restrictions; and direction from security forces, traffic controllers, or emergency personnel. Civilian drivers operating privately owned vehicles on JBA are subject to Maryland traffic laws, and installation driving privileges may be affected by traffic violations. af.mil
The National Capital Region presents elevated driving hazards due to dense traffic, frequent lane changes, aggressive or distracted drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, buses, emergency vehicles, road construction, and limited parking. Drivers will maintain situational awareness, avoid distracted driving, use hands-free communication only when permitted, wear seat belts, maintain safe following distances, and adjust speed and vehicle operation for traffic, weather, visibility, and road conditions.
Personnel operating in Washington, DC, must pay particular attention to pedestrians, cyclists, crosswalks, bike lanes, automated traffic enforcement areas, and lower speed limits. Unless otherwise posted, the District’s maximum lawful speed is 20 mph; lower limits may apply near schools, playgrounds, alleys, or other specially marked areas. 
When traveling in Maryland or Virginia, personnel should exercise caution near stopped emergency vehicles, disabled vehicles, roadside workers, and work zones. Maryland’s Move Over Law requires drivers to move over or slow down when approaching stopped vehicles displaying warning signals. Virginia similarly requires drivers to move over when safe or slow down for stopped vehicles and pedestrians; Virginia also identifies work zones as areas requiring reduced speed, increased following distance, and heightened awareness of workers and equipment. 
Personnel will not operate a vehicle while impaired, fatigued, distracted, or otherwise unable to drive safely. Drivers will use only authorized parking areas, comply with base speed limits and pedestrian right-of-way requirements, avoid blocking fire lanes or emergency access routes, and immediately report vehicle accidents, injuries, or hazardous road conditions through the appropriate installation, local law-enforcement, or supervisory channels.
On-Base Traffic and Pedestrian Safety — Joint Base Andrews
Personnel operating vehicles, bicycles, or traveling as pedestrians on Joint Base Andrews will comply with all posted traffic control devices, installation rules, and instructions from Security Forces or traffic-control personnel. 
JBA personnel should anticipate congestion, delays, and changing traffic patterns near installation gates, during peak arrival and departure periods, weather events, construction, special events, and heightened security conditions. Gate hours and access procedures may change; personnel should check current JBA information before travel and allow sufficient time to reach their duty location safely. 

•	Speed Limits: The installation speed limit is 25 mph unless otherwise posted. Parking-lot speed limits are generally 5–10 mph, or as posted. Drivers will reduce speed when approaching intersections, crosswalks, parking areas, pedestrians, cyclists, and congested work areas.
•	Pedestrian Safety: Pedestrians will use designated sidewalks, crosswalks, and marked pedestrian routes when available. Before entering a roadway or crossing a parking lot, pedestrians will remain alert for moving vehicles and make eye contact with drivers when practical. Drivers will yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and exercise added caution near building entrances, parking areas, and fitness areas.
•	Headphones and Earpieces: The use of headphones or earpieces is authorized only while using the base gym or running track. Personnel will not wear headphones or earpieces while walking, running, cycling, operating vehicles, or performing duties in areas where situational awareness is required.
•	Bicycle Safety: Bicycle riders will wear required personal protective equipment and use reflective belts or other high-visibility equipment during periods of low visibility, including darkness, dawn, dusk, or inclement weather. Cyclists will obey all traffic signs, signals, and right-of-way requirements and remain alert for vehicle and pedestrian traffic.
•	Installation Gates and Active Vehicle Barriers: Joint Base Andrews access points include the Main Gate on the north side of the installation, Pearl Harbor Gate on the east side, and Virginia Gate on the south side. Gate areas contain emergency pop-up vehicle barriers. Drivers must remain alert for posted signs, signals, and instructions indicating potential barrier activation. Do not attempt to rush through a gate or cross a barrier when it is being activated. A yellow warning light indicates that the barrier is about to activate. Drivers will approach all barriers cautiously, maintain adequate spacing from the vehicle ahead, and never stop a vehicle on top of a barrier.
